headline: Schneider Electric has agreed to buy the US industrial software maker PTC for $22.6 billion in cash, its largest acquisition so far.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: a very large announced deal, confirmed by the companies.
importance_line: What changed is that a European electrical-equipment giant is buying the software used to design factory products, which matters to manufacturers that depend on that software, then to PTC shareholders, then to rivals such as Siemens, and the doubt is that regulators have yet to approve it and Schneider's own shares fell after the news.
summary: Schneider Electric said on Monday 5 Oct that it will buy PTC, a Boston company whose software is used to design, build and service industrial products, for $205 a share in cash, a 42.3% premium to Friday's close, with completion expected by the third quarter of 2027 subject to regulatory approval, according to a Stocktwits report carried by TradingView and the New York Post's account of Reuters and Financial Times reporting; the Financial Times first reported the talks on Sunday. Schneider plans to pay with up to 6 billion euros of new shares and up to 17 billion euros of debt, its shares fell about 7% to 8% in Paris while PTC's jumped, and its forecast of about 250 million euros a year in cost savings is the company's own claim.
notes: Reuters article (pool item) could not be read; entry built from several outlets and labelled AI News Desk. Talks were first reported by the Financial Times on 4 Oct 2026; the announcement was 5 Oct 2026.
